'''The big theme: your "sequential misc" idea is the key.''' Most of what's below has been stuck in "unregistered, run by hand" for '''one reason''': the daily drip runs lines in '''random order''', which is unsafe for any remove-then-add or add-then-remove pair (the remove could fire first and leave a shrine blank). A '''sequential misc''' — a file that runs top-to-bottom, one edit per run, never interleaved — makes every such pair safe and un-sticks all of it. It needs a small design (it changes how the daily editor picks lines) but it is the right answer. Say the word and I'll design it.

:* '''84 are the same shrine as two items''' — one item for the living shrine, a separate item for the 927 register entry, and the list names the register-entry one. So the living-shrine item only ''looks'' unnamed because its twin is the one on the list. Matched three ways: shared Kokugakuin id, identical Japanese name, or old-vs-new kanji spelling. '''Your call:''' link the 84 pairs ("these two are the same shrine") or merge them.
:* '''66 have no twin''' — either modern shrines mis-tagged as register entries, or genuine entries the lists are missing. '''Your call:''' which. I can hand you the full 84 + 66 as a browsable table.

'''Kokugakuin id matcher''' — you asked for more context.
: '''→''' Every real 927 register entry has an id in the Kokugakuin University shrine database; some of your entry items are missing it. The matcher tries to fill it by matching the shrine's name against the database's entry titles. The catch: name-matching alone isn't safe — two adjacent database entries can describe the same shrine, so a name match can attach the ''wrong'' id. It cut the missing-id set from 94 to 18 but found '''zero''' safe to add on its own. '''Your call:''' is name-matching good enough, or do the 18 need per-item eyes? Nothing runs until you say.
